d: Internal square, to which they put several small streets. At the end of the canal; a bridge crosses it, from which you go down into the square. Palaces, and houses of all around, to the left the house of Maffeo, well ahead. It is night. They advance cautiously from the streets some People wrapped in the capes, join, and speak subtlely, observing the square; then Luigi, finally Foscari.

Interior of the house of the Bravo, in a remote district of Venice. A low open window from which you can see the sky, at the bottom of the gulf. Slow steps you can see entering a man dressed in black, with a mask on his face and with a dagger on his belt. He stops: he is the Bravo. Then Pisani.

The square of St. Mark. In perspective the outside of the temple with front the three golden bronze pedestals, with above the flags of the three kingdoms Cyprus, Candia, Morea. On one side the door of the ducal palace. Laterally the Procuratie. Coffee shops. Jewellers. Orefici. Merchants of all sorts. The bell tower to the right. The scene is full of People rushed to the feast of the solemn day, and to the appearance of the Doge and the Signoria. Citizens, Artiers, Noble, Greeks, Dalmatians, Masks. Dames and Knights, overlooking the windows of the procuratie. At the sound of festive march the Dalmatine Guards, the Uscieri, the Senators, the Heads of the Council of the Forties, the Knights from the Golden Stole. Finally, the Doge in pompous disguise followed by Paggi. Plausi, acclamations, sounds on each side.
The Bravo in Dalmatian noble dress, then Foscari.
From the door of the clock comes out unordinarily running the People, then Marco, Michelina, Cappello with other Nobili; at the time Violetta, finally Pisani.
Cabinet in the palace of Teodora. Teodora dressed simply, then Michelina and Marco.
Room in the house of the Bravo as in act I. Violetta sleeping in the adjoining room. The Bravo looks at it with emotion.

Room in the palace of Teodora beautifully decorated for the dance party and banquet. The architecture is fantastic, it has a mixture of Greek and Gothic used at those times, mostly in Venice. The wardrobes of the hall are of the same kind. The hall on the front of the theater has the entrance from a great arch, from which hang wide curtains of golden drapes; the columns are crowned with flowers. On the sides of the arcade two galleries for music. Beyond the arcade you can see another room decorated with other taste. Bizarre lamps and faces of each around. Golden candles are seen in the adjoining hall. Silver and gold vases: luxury shines from every side. Up the scene, little by little from the last rooms of S'avanzano Dame, Gentilumini with mask and without, that look around with enthusiasm. The music begins. All are dressed in different costumes.
All the Knights go out before and after Violetta accompanied by the Bravo masked by Greek; it is veiled to the feet.
Teodora's Cabinet. Teodora in modest dress, sitting, leaning on a table, Michelina, who is waiting for her notes, then Violetta.
Michelina enters and announces the Bravo, who follows her, then Pisani.

A remote place in the district of Castello. A cenobe with adjoining Gothic temple. To the right a house under a porch. View of the lagoon, at the bottom of the lido. Islets here and there, some lights in the distance. The moon is among the clouds: to the left you go down two or three steps in the canal. They advance in groups, slowly, Guards, and Night Sculptures.
The Bravo comes out anxiously and anxiously, then Teodora and Violetta.
Pisani, who was hidden, comes out suddenly.
